tex_content.html:
Lemma
[synchronized finite chart partition for two curves]

If $\gamma :[0,1]\to M$ and $\tilde\gamma :[0,1]\to \tilde M$ are continuous, then there are a monotone partition $0=\tau _0\leq \tau _1\leq \cdots $ which is eventually equal to $1$, and charts $\alpha _i$ on $M$ and $\tilde\alpha _i$ on $\tilde M$, such that each closed piece $[\tau _i,\tau _{i+1}]$ is mapped by $\gamma $ into the source of $\alpha _i$ and by $\tilde\gamma $ into the source of $\tilde\alpha _i$. Thus both curves have a common finite subdivision by one-chart pieces.
Proof

Apply the compactness lemma to the open cover of $[0,1]$ by the intersections of the pullbacks of chart sources along $\gamma $ and $\tilde\gamma $.

□
